newsitem.title: UK: Siemens looking for defence partner - paper.
newsitem.headline: Siemens looking for defence partner - paper.

text.p: German engineering giant Siemens AG, is looking for a partner or buyer for its defence electronics business in response to cuts in government spending and difficulties with funding larger programmes, said the Financial Times on Friday.
The FT said the group had told its 5000 employees, most of whom are UK-based, that if it does not find a suitable partner it has not discounted the option of divesting.

Its Siemens Plessey division faced a setback this month when the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) cancelled an order for electronic warfare systems after the company had spent 50 million stg on development.
Possible buyers of the Siemens unit could include General Electric Company Plc and Racal Electronics.
Siemens Plessey is also in the running for the two billion stg UK MOD Bowman battlefield radio contract as part of a wider consortium.

An announcement on the winner of that contract could come soon and is expected to yield an extra two billion stg of export orders from other countries on top of the contract value itself for the winning team.
